title: Alzheimer disease and frontotemporal dementia

steps.tx: **Alzheimer disease** neuropathology is defined by extracellular amyloid-beta **42** senile plaques and intracellular **neurofibrillary tangles** composed of hyperphosphorylated tau protein. Neuropathological progression begins in the transentorhinal cortex and hippocampus before disseminating diffusely across neocortical association areas throughout cerebral hemispheres in affected individuals.

steps.tx: Early-onset familial Alzheimer disease is caused by autosomal dominant mutations in APP on chromosome **21**, **presenilin** 1 (PSEN1 on chromosome **14**), and PSEN2 on chromosome **1**, while **APOE** epsilon-4 on chromosome **19** is the major genetic risk factor for late-onset disease.
steps.say: Early-onset familial Alzheimer disease is caused by autosomal dominant mutations in APP on chromosome 21 presenilin 1 PSEN1 on chromosome 14 and PSEN2 on chromosome 1 while APOE epsilon-4 on chromosome 19 is the major genetic risk factor for late-onset disease.

rows: Onset age 45 to 60, prominent amyloid angiopathy
Onset age 30 to 50, most common familial mutation
Onset age 40 to 70, variable clinical penetrance
Major genetic risk factor for sporadic late-onset AD

steps.tx: CSF and plasma biomarkers for Alzheimer disease demonstrate decreased **amyloid-beta** **42/40** ratio accompanied by elevated levels of **phosphorylated tau** (p-tau**181**, p-tau**217**). Decreased fluid amyloid reflects sequestration into parenchymal plaques while soluble p-tau mirrors active neurofibrillary tangle formation across cerebral regions.

left.title: Amyloid Biomarkers
points: Positive cortical amyloid binding on florbetapir PET

right.title: Tau & Neurodegeneration Markers
points: Elevated total tau reflecting axonal injury
Hippocampal volume loss on volumetric MRI

steps.tx: Behavioral variant **frontotemporal dementia** presents with early **disinhibition**, apathy, loss of empathy, hyperorality, and compulsive stereotyped behaviours associated with focal frontal and anterior temporal atrophy on structural and functional neuroimaging acquisitions in affected middle-aged individuals presenting to specialized outpatient memory clinics.

steps.tx: Semantic variant **primary progressive aphasia** features progressive loss of word meaning and object knowledge with profound **confrontation naming** impairment with preserved fluency, linked to anterior inferior temporal lobe atrophy predominantly on the left cerebral hemisphere in clinical cohorts undergoing language evaluations.

left.title: Semantic Variant PPA
points: Asymmetric left anterior inferior temporal atrophy

steps.tx: **Normal pressure hydrocephalus** presents with the classic **Hakim-Adams** triad of gait apraxia (magnetic gait), urinary incontinence, and progressive cognitive impairment, showing ventriculomegaly disproportionate to sulcal enlargement (DESH) on magnetic resonance imaging across serial axial and coronal cuts in affected elderly patients.

left.title: Hakim-Adams Triad
points: Urinary urgency, frequency, and frank incontinence
Subcortical cognitive slowing and executive deficit
Gait disturbance almost universally appears first

right.title: DESH Neuroimaging Signs
points: Enlarged Sylvian fissures with callosal angle <90 degrees

steps.tx: High-volume therapeutic **lumbar puncture** spinal tap test with **30** to **50** mL cerebrospinal fluid removal that produces objective **gait velocity** improvement confirms shunt-responsiveness in normal pressure hydrocephalus prior to definitive surgical ventriculoperitoneal shunt placement in specialist neurosurgical clinics evaluating prospective shunt candidates.
steps.say: High-volume therapeutic lumbar puncture tap test with 30 to 50 mL removal that produces objective gait velocity improvement confirms shunt-responsiveness in normal pressure hydrocephalus prior to ventriculoperitoneal shunt placement in specialist neurosurgical clinics.

left.title: Diagnostic Tap Test
points: Removal of 30 to 50 mL cerebrospinal fluid
Re-evaluation of gait velocity at 2 to 4 hours

right.title: Surgical Shunt Outcome
points: Gait improvement observed in >80% of responders
Dementia least likely to completely reverse

steps.tx: Anti-amyloid monoclonal antibodies including **lecanemab** and **donanemab** clear cerebral amyloid-beta plaques in early symptomatic Alzheimer disease, requiring MRI surveillance for amyloid-related imaging abnormalities such as vasogenic edema (ARIA-E) and sulcal microhemorrhages (ARIA-H) throughout scheduled dosing regimens in specialized neurocognitive infusion centers.

left.title: Mechanism of Action
points: Target soluble amyloid protofibrils and plaques
Significant reduction in amyloid burden on PET

right.title: ARIA Surveillance Protocols
points: Baseline brain MRI before initiating therapy
Serial MRI monitoring before infusions 5, 7, and 14
ARIA-E: sulcal and parenchymal vasogenic edema
